body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Omniscient One!

children.text: kṛtsnasya tantrasya gṛhītadhāmnaś cikitsitād viprasṛtasya dūram /
children.translated_text: Of the entire treatise whose essence has been grasped, which has gone far beyond the <s>Cikitsita</s> (therapeutics section),
which is honored by skilled physicians — a compilation of the <s>Yogaśataka</s> (Hundred Formulations) shall be made.
Having examined the causes, diseases, and symptoms, by a physician who knows therapeutics,

children.text: nirāmadehasya hi bhaiṣajāni bhavanti yuktāny amṛtopamāni // Yś_2 //
children.translated_text: medicines for the body freed from <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) become efficacious, like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar).

With <s>chinnodbhava</s> (Achyranthes aspera), <s>ambudhara</s> (Cyperus rotundus), <s>dhanvayavāsa</s> (Fagonia cretica), <s>viśva</s> (dry ginger), <s>duḥsparśa</s> (Mucuna pruriens), <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>megha</s> (Cyperus), <s>kirātatikta</s> (Swertia chirata),

<s>mustā</s>, <s>aṭarūṣaka</s> (Adhatoda vasica), <s>mahauṣadha</s> (dry ginger), <s>dhanvayāsa</s> — one should drink the decoction in fevers of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm).

A decoction made with <s>kṣudrā</s> (small caltrops), <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora cordifolia), <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger), and <s>puṣkarāhvaya</s> (Inula racemosa) — for fevers predominated by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
with dyspnea, cough, loss of appetite, and side pain, it is recommended even in fevers arising from all three <s>doṣas</s>.
A decoction boiled with <s>āragvadha</s> (Cassia fistula), <s>granthika</s> (Piper longum root), <s>mustā</s>, <s>tiktā</s> (Solanum indicum), and <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula) —

children.text: sāme saśūle kaphavātayukte jvare hito dīpanapācanaś ca // Yś_5 //
children.translated_text: is beneficial in fever with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and colic combined with <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and it promotes digestion and appetizing.
One should prepare a decoction of <s>drākṣā</s> (grape), <s>abhayā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>abda</s> (Cyperus rotundus), and <s>tiktā</s>, with <s>śamyāka</s> fruit,
for fever arising from <s>pitta</s> accompanied by delirium, fainting, dizziness, burning, confusion, and thirst.
One should drink a decoction of <s>nidigdhikā</s> (Solanum xanthocarpum), <s>nāgara</s>, <s>kā</s> (long pepper), and <s>amṛtā</s>, mixed with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper),
for chronic fever, loss of appetite, cough, colic, dyspnea, weak digestive fire, facial paralysis, and rhinitis.

Of <s>durālabhā</s> (Fagonia cretica), <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s> (Callicarpa macrophylla), <s>bhūnimba</s> (Andrographis paniculata), <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda vasica), and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (Picrorhiza kurroa) —
one should drink the decoction deeply mixed with sugar, when afflicted with thirst, bleeding, <s>pitta</s> fever, and burning.

Having boiled <s>phalatrika</s> (the three fruits — triphala), <s>dāru</s> (Cedrus deodara), <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), <s>viśālā</s> (Trichosanthes), and <s>musta</s>, making a paste of the <s>niśā</s> portion,

children.text: pibet kaṣāyaṃ madhusaṃprayuktaṃ sarvaprameheṣu samutthiteṣu // Yś_9 //
children.translated_text: one should drink this decoction mixed with honey for all types of <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders) that have arisen.

children.text: savatsakaḥ sātiviṣaḥ sabilvaḥ sodīcyamustaś ca kṛtaḥ kaṣāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: A decoction made with <s>vatsaka</s> (Holarrhena antidysenterica), <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum heterophyllum), <s>bilva</s> (Aegle marmelos), <s>udīcyamusta</s> (northern Cyperus) —

children.text: sāme saśūle ca saśoṇite ca cirapravṛtte 'pi hito 'tisāre // Yś_10 //
children.translated_text: is beneficial in <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhea), even when chronic, whether with <s>āma</s>, with colic, or with blood.

children.text: śuṇṭhīṃ samustātiviṣāguḍūcīṃ pibej jalena kvathitāṃ samāṃśām /
children.translated_text: One should drink <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger) with <s>mustā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora cordifolia), boiled in water in equal parts,

children.text: mandānalatve satatāmayānām āmānubandhe grahaṇīgade ca // Yś_11 //
children.translated_text: for weak digestive fire in persistent diseases with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), and in <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) disease.
One should drink <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>abhayā</s>, and <s>guḍūcī</s> with urine, mixed with <s>mahiṣākṣa</s> (Embelia ribes),
for skin disorders, edema, abdominal disease, <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> (anemia), obesity, urethral discharge, and upward-moving <s>kapha</s> diseases.

A decoction of <s>mustā</s>, <s>ākhuparṇī</s>, <s>phala</s> (Randia dumetorum), <s>dāru</s>, and <s>śigru</s> (Moringa oleifera), with a paste of <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (black pepper) and <s>kṛmiśatru</s> (Embelia ribes) —

children.text: mārgadvayenāpi cirapravṛttān kṛmīn nihanyāt kṛmijāṃś ca rogān // Yś_13 //
children.translated_text: destroys worms by both pathways, even those long established, and diseases born of worms.

With <s>elā</s> (cardamom), <s>upakulyā</s>, <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>aśmabheda</s> (Bergenia ligulata), <s>kauntī</s>, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (Tribulus terrestris), <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda vasica), and <s>korubūka</s>,

children.text: śṛtaṃ pibed aśmajatupradhānaṃ saśarkare sāśmarimūtrakṛcchre // Yś_14 //
children.translated_text: one should drink the cooked preparation with <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) as the chief ingredient, for <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary calculus) and <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (difficult urination) with sugar disease.
Having drunk the powders of <s>elā</s>, <s>aśmabheda</s>, <s>śilājatu</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>, ground with rice-water,

children.text: yad vā guḍena sahitāny avalehyamānāny āsannamṛtyur api jīvati mūtrakṛcchrī // Yś_15 //
children.translated_text: or having licked them mixed with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), even one near death suffering from <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> will live.
Of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>gokṣura</s> (Tribulus terrestris), <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> (Cassia fistula), <s>pāṣāṇabhid</s> (Bergenia ligulata), and <s>dhanvayavāsaka</s> —

children.text: kvāthaṃ piben mākṣikasaṃprayuktaṃ kṛcchre sadāhe saruje vibandhe // Yś_16 //
children.translated_text: one should drink the decoction mixed with honey for <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> with burning, pain, and obstruction.
One should drink a decoction of <s>vāsā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s> (Trapa bispinosa) with castor oil;

children.text: krameṇa sarvāṅgajam apy aśeṣaṃ jayed asṛgvātabhavaṃ vikāram // Yś_17 //
children.translated_text: gradually it will conquer entirely all conditions born of blood and <s>vāta</s> affecting the whole body.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> (Berberis extract) and the root of <s>taṇḍulaka</s> (Amaranthus), drunk with honey and rice-water,

children.text: asṛgdaraṃ sarvabhavaṃ nihanti śvāsaṃ ca bhārgī saha nāgareṇa // Yś_18 //
children.translated_text: destroys bleeding of every type; and <s>bhārgī</s> (Clerodendrum serratum) with <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger) destroys dyspnea.

A decoction made with <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), <s>bilva</s>, the two <s>bṛhatīs</s> (Solanum indicum and S. xanthocarpum), <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron), <s>pāṣāṇabhid</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s> (the three pungents), and roots —
mixed with <s>kṣāra</s> (alkali), <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), salt, and sesame oil — should be drunk for pains in the hips, shoulders, pelvis, heart, and breasts.

<s>Hiṅgu</s>, <s>ugragandhā</s> (Acorus calamus), <s>viḍa</s> salt, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>ajājī</s> (cumin), <s>harītakī</s>, <s>puṣkaramūla</s> (Inula racemosa root), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea lappa) —

children.text: bhāgottaraṃ cūrṇitam etad iṣṭaṃ gulmodarājīrṇavisūcikāsu // Yś_20 //
children.translated_text: powdered with each increasing in proportion — this is beneficial for <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), <s>udara</s> (abdominal disease), indigestion, and <s>visūcikā</s> (cholera).
Equal powder of <s>rucaka</s> salt, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>mahauṣadha</s> (dry ginger) — for conditions of the heart, sides, back, and abdomen and <s>visūcikā</s> arising from <s>kapha</s> and wind,

children.text: hṛtpārśvapṛṣṭhajaṭharārtivisūcikāsu peyaṃ tathā yavarasena ca viḍvibandhe // Yś_21 //
children.translated_text: it should be drunk with dry ginger water; and with barley juice for fecal obstruction.
<s>Pūtīkapatra</s>, <s>gajacirbiṭa</s> (Cucumis), <s>cavya</s> (Piper chaba), <s>agni</s> (Plumbago zeylanica), <s>trikaṭu</s>, layered with salt placed on top —

children.text: dagdhvā vicūrṇya dadhimastuyutaṃ prayojyaṃ gulmodaraśvayathupāṇḍugudodbhaveṣu // Yś_22 //
children.translated_text: burnt and powdered, mixed with yogurt whey, it should be applied for <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, edema, anemia, and rectal disorders.

children.text: dviruttarā hiṅgu vacā sakuṣṭhā suvarcikā ceti viḍaṃ ca cūrṇam /
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgu</s>, <s>vacā</s> (Acorus calamus), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> — each doubled in succession — <s>suvarcikā</s> (black salt), and <s>viḍa</s> salt; this powder,
with hot water, destroys flatulence, <s>visūcikā</s>, pain, heart disease, <s>gulma</s>, and upward-moving wind.

<s>Śṛṅgī</s> (Pistacia integerrima), the three pungents, the three fruits, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> (Solanum xanthocarpum), <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>puṣkara</s> (Inula racemosa), <s>jaṭā</s> (spikenard), and the five salts —

children.text: cūrṇaṃ pibed aśiśireṇa jalena hikkāśvāsordhvavātakasanārucipīnaseṣu // Yś_24 //
children.translated_text: one should drink this powder with warm water for hiccup, dyspnea, upward-moving wind, acid reflux, loss of appetite, and rhinitis.
<s>Nādeyī</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s> (Holarrhena), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>śigru</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>snuk</s> (Euphorbia), <s>bilva</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s> (Semecarpus),
<s>vyāghrī</s> (Solanum), <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Butea monosperma), <s>pāribhadraka</s> (Erythrina), <s>jaṭā</s>, <s>pāmārga</s> (Achyranthes), <s>nīpa</s> (Anthocephalus), <s>agni</s> (Plumbago),
<s>vāsā</s>, <s>muṣkaka</s>, and <s>pāṭalā</s> (Stereospermum) — with salt, burnt, and the juice cooked
with <s>hiṅgvādi</s> seasoning — this is suitable for <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, and splenic disorders.

With equal parts of <s>cavya</s>, <s>amlavetasa</s> (Garcinia pedunculata), the three pungents, <s>tittiḍīka</s> (tamarind), <s>tālīsa</s> (Abies webbiana), <s>jīraka</s> (cumin), <s>tugā</s>, and <s>dahana</s> (Plumbago) —

children.text: cūrṇaṃ guḍapramṛditaṃ trisugandhiyuktaṃ vaisvaryapīnasakaphāruciṣu praśastam // Yś_26 //
children.translated_text: powder mixed with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) and the three aromatics — excellent for hoarseness, rhinitis, <s>kapha</s>, and loss of appetite.

children.text: tālīsacavyamaricaṃ sadṛśaṃ dviraṃśaṃ mūlaṃ tugāṃ magadhajāṃ triguṇāṃ ca śuṇṭhīm /
children.translated_text: Equal parts of <s>tālīsa</s>, <s>cavya</s>, and <s>marica</s> (black pepper); double the portion of <s>tugā</s> root; triple of <s>magadhajā</s> (long pepper); and triple of <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger) —

children.text: kṛtvā guḍatriguṇitāṃ guḍikāṃ sugandhāṃ kāsāgnimāndyagudajajvararukṣu dadyāt // Yś_27 //
children.translated_text: making a fragrant pill with triple the amount of <s>guḍa</s> — one should give it for cough, weak digestion, rectal disorders, and feverish pain.

<s>Śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), <s>marica</s>, <s>nāgadala</s> (cinnamon leaf), <s>tvak</s> (cinnamon bark), and <s>elā</s> (cardamom) — powdered, each increasing in proportion upward from the last;
one should eat this with equal sugar for rectal disorders, weak digestion, <s>gulma</s>, loss of appetite, dyspnea, and throat and heart diseases.
One should make a pill with <s>sindhūttha</s> (rock salt), <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (the three fruits), <s>yavānī</s> (Trachyspermum ammi), <s>trikaṭu</s>, and equal parts of <s>guḍa</s>;

children.text: tair bhakṣitais tṛptim avāpnuvan na bhuñjīta mandāgnir api prabhūtam // Yś_29 //
children.translated_text: by eating these, even one with weak digestion shall gain satisfaction without experiencing fullness, and may eat abundantly.
Equal parts of iron, <s>tila</s> (sesame), <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> (the three pungents), and <s>kola</s> (jujube); an equal amount of iron-powder mixed with honey —

children.text: tair modakaḥ kṣaudrayuto 'nutakraḥ pāṇḍvāmaye dūragate 'pi śastaḥ // Yś_30 //
children.translated_text: pills with honey and buttermilk are beneficial for <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia) disease, even when far advanced.

children.text: guḍena śuṇṭhīm athavopakulyāṃ pathyātṛtīyām atha dāḍimaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: One should always eat <s>śuṇṭhī</s> with <s>guḍa</s>, or <s>upakulyā</s> with <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula) as the third, and also <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) —

children.text: āmeṣv ajīrṇeṣu gudāmayeṣu varcovibandheṣu ca nityam adyāt // Yś_31 //
children.translated_text: for <s>āma</s> conditions, indigestion, rectal disorders, and fecal obstruction.
Powder of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, and <s>mustā</s> — pills should be made with <s>guḍa</s>;

children.text: nivārayaty āsyavidhāriteyaṃ śvāsaṃ pravṛddhaṃ prabalaṃ ca kāsam // Yś_32 //
children.translated_text: held in the mouth, this suppresses aggravated dyspnea and severe cough.

children.text: vaṭaprarohaṃ madhu kuṣṭham utpalaṃ salājacūrṇaṃ guḍikāṃ prakalpayet /
children.translated_text: One should prepare pills from aerial roots of <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan), honey, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and parched grain powder;

children.text: susaṃhitā sā vadanena dhāritā tṛṣṇāṃ pravṛddhām api hanti satvaram // Yś_33 //
children.translated_text: well-prepared and held in the mouth, it quickly destroys even severe thirst.
Powder of <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), <s>māgadhī</s> (long pepper), and <s>uṣṇa</s> (dry ginger), mixed with the sour juice of <s>kapittha</s> (wood apple),

children.text: lājaiḥ samāṃśair madhunāvalīḍhaṃ chardiṃ prasaktām asakṛn nihanti // Yś_34 //
children.translated_text: with equal parts of parched grain, licked with honey — it destroys persistent vomiting repeatedly.

children.text: dūrvāraso dāḍimapuṣpajo vā ghrāṇapravṛtte 'sṛji nasyam uktam /
children.translated_text: Juice of <s>dūrvā</s> (Cynodon grass) or that produced from <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) flowers is prescribed as nasal drops for nosebleed;

children.text: stanyena vālaktarasena vāpi viṇ makṣikānāṃ ca nihanti hikkām // Yś_35 //
children.translated_text: with breast milk or with <s>lākṣā</s> (lac) juice, and the excrement of flies — it destroys hiccup.

children.text: dhātrīrasaḥ sarjarasaḥ sapākyaḥ sauvīrapiṣṭaś ca tadāsutaś ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātrī</s> (amla) juice, <s>sarja</s> (Vateria indica) resin with <s>pākya</s>, <s>sauvīra</s> (vinegar) paste and its extract —

children.text: bhavanti sidhmāni yathā na bhūyas tathaivam udvartanakaṃ karoti // Yś_36 //
children.translated_text: make an exfoliant so that <s>sidhmā</s> (skin patches) do not recur.
<s>Dūrvā</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>cakramarda</s> (Cassia tora), and <s>kuṭheraka</s> — pasted with fermented rice-water and buttermilk;

children.text: tribhiḥ pralepair api baddhamūlāṃ dadruṃ ca kaṇḍuṃ ca vināśayanti // Yś_37 //
children.translated_text: with three applications, they destroy even deeply-rooted ringworm and itching.
With <s>gaṇḍīrika</s>, <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica), <s>mārka</s>, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>kuṣṭha</s>, tree bark, and salts, with urine —
one should cook oil; it removes circular skin disease, ringworm, chronic wounds, pain, and <s>kiṭima</s> (scaly skin disease).
This pungent oil, cooked with equal parts of <s>sindūra</s> (red lead), <s>guggulu</s> (Commiphora mukul), <s>rasāñjana</s>, <s>siktha</s> (beeswax), and <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate) —

children.text: kacchūṃ sravatpiṭakikām athavāpi śuṣkām abhyañjanena sakṛd uddharati prasahya // Yś_39 //
children.translated_text: by a single application, forcefully removes itching, whether oozing pustules or dry ones.
With <s>suvarcikā</s> (black salt), <s>nāgara</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>mūrvā</s> (Marsdenia tenacissima), <s>lākṣā</s>, <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), and <s>lohitayaṣṭikā</s> (Abrus precatorius) —

children.text: tailaṃ jvare ṣaḍguṇatakrasiddham abhyañjanāc chītavidāhanut syāt // Yś_40 //
children.translated_text: oil prepared with six times the amount of buttermilk — by application, it would relieve cold and burning sensations in fever.

children.text: sarpir guḍūcīvṛṣakaṇṭakārīkvāthena kalkena ca siddham etat /
children.translated_text: Ghee prepared with the decoction and paste of <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> —
should be drunk for chronic fever, cough, colic, dyspnea, weak digestion, and <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) disease.
With the decoction and paste of <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu), <s>paṭola</s> leaf, <s>nimba</s> (neem) bark, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry) —

children.text: ghṛtam abhinavam etad āśu siddhaṃ jayati visarpamadāśrakuṣṭhagulmān // Yś_42 //
children.translated_text: this fresh ghee, quickly prepared, conquers <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), intoxication, blood disorders, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), and <s>gulma</s>.
<s>Visarpa</s> (erysipelas) is produced by <s>doṣas</s> aggravated in the skin, flesh, and blood;
it is a type of wasting affecting the entire body, a special form of <s>visarpa</s>.
Intoxication (<s>mada</s>) is of the nature of liquor — a disorder produced by the drinking of liquor. // Yś_43 //

With waters of <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>picumarda</s> (neem), <s>dhāvanī</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), and <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda) in paste form,

children.text: ghṛtam uttamaṃ vidhivipakvam ādṛtaḥ prapibann idaṃ jayati kuṣṭham āturaḥ // Yś_44 //
children.translated_text: ghee of the finest quality, properly cooked according to procedure — the afflicted one who drinks this with care conquers skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). // Yś_44 //
Pieces of <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s> (white gourd), steamed by the cooking method, dried, and fried in ghee —

one should add, when the sugar is cooked, equal parts of black pepper (<s>marica</s>), long pepper (<s>magadhā</s>), dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), cumin (<s>ajājī</s>), and the three aromatics (<s>trigandha</s>);
this electuary (<s>leha</s>) is beneficial for children, the elderly, those afflicted by wind and blood disorders, the emaciated, women, those with consumption (<s>kṣata</s>),
and for those suffering from thirst, cough, bleeding disorders, <s>pitta</s> (bile), dyspnea, abdominal disease, pain, and vomiting. // Yś_45 //
Having cooked urine, sour gruel, and honey with <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum), <s>piṇḍītaka</s>, black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), <s>viḍa</s> salt, <s>dhūma</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea),

children.text: vartiṃ karāṅguṣṭhanibhāṃ ghṛtāktāṃ gude rujānāhaharīṃ vidadhyāt // Yś_46 //
children.translated_text: one should prepare a suppository the size of a thumb, smeared with ghee, to be placed in the rectum to relieve pain and distension. // Yś_46 //

children.text: saśarkaraṃ kuṅkumam ājyabhṛṣṭaṃ nasyaṃ vidheyaṃ pavanāsṛgutthe /
children.translated_text: Saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>) mixed with sugar and fried in ghee should be administered as nasal medication (<s>nasya</s>) in conditions arising from wind and blood disorders —
in pain of the brow, ear, temple, eye, and half-head (hemicrania), and in diseases that increase day by day. // Yś_47 //

With the seeds of <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia bellirica), and <s>dhātrī</s> (Emblica) fruit, in proportions of three, two, and one parts, one should prepare a collyrium stick (<s>varti</s>);

children.text: tayāñjayed aśrum atipravṛddham akṣṇor haret kaṣṭam api prakopam // Yś_48 //
children.translated_text: applied as eye ointment, it removes excessive tearing and eliminates even severe inflammation of the eyes. // Yś_48 //
With <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s> (mineral earth),

children.text: bahiṣpralepaṃ nayanasya kuryāt sarvākṣirogopaśamārtham etat // Yś_49 //
children.translated_text: and <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), ground in clear water, one should apply an external paste to the eye — this is for the alleviation of all eye diseases. // Yś_49 //
<s>Lodhra</s> (Symplocos) mixed with rock salt and fried in ghee, ground with <s>sauvīra</s> (antimony), tied in a white cloth —

children.text: āścyotanaṃ tan nayanasya kuryāt sadāhakaṇḍūṃ ca rujaṃ nihanyāt // Yś_50 //
children.translated_text: one should use that as an eye wash (<s>āścyotana</s>) for the eye; it destroys burning sensation, itching, and pain. // Yś_50 //

children.text: hanty arjunaṃ śarkarayābdhipheno naktāndhatāṃ gośakṛtā ca kṛṣṇā /
children.translated_text: Sea foam (<s>abdhiphena</s>) with sugar destroys <s>arjuna</s> (pterygium); black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>) with cow dung destroys night blindness;

children.text: rasāñjanaṃ vyoṣayutaṃ ca pillaṃ tāpīsamutthaṃ madhunā ca śukram // Yś_51 //
children.translated_text: <s>rasāñjana</s> (extract of Berberis) combined with the three pungents (<s>vyoṣa</s>) [destroys] <s>pilla</s> (membrane growth); that which arises from the <s>Tāpī</s> river with honey [destroys] <s>śukra</s> (corneal opacity). // Yś_51 //

With equal parts of <s>puṣpākhya</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, white sea foam (<s>udadhiphena</s>), conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), <s>sindhūttha</s> (rock salt), <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), and black pepper (<s>marica</s>),

children.text: piṣṭais tu mākṣikarasena rasakriyeyaṃ hanty armakācatimirārjunavartmarogān // Yś_52 //
children.translated_text: ground and made into a collyrium preparation (<s>rasakriyā</s>) with honey — this destroys <s>arman</s> (pterygium), <s>kāca</s> (cataract), <s>timira</s> (dimness of vision), <s>arjuna</s> (pterygium), and <s>vartman</s> (eyelid) diseases. // Yś_52 //
<s>Musta</s> (Cyperus), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), <s>rajas</s> (turmeric), barley (<s>yava</s>), <s>āsa</s>, and black pepper (<s>marica</s>), rock salt (<s>sindhūdbhava</s>), <s>kaṭphala</s> (Myrica),
<s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), conch shell (<s>śaṅkhaphena</s>), <s>nalada</s> (spikenard), <s>kālānusārī</s> (dark fragrant substance), and collyrium (<s>añjana</s>) —

children.text: tulyaṃ cūrṇitam āyase vinihitaṃ kṣaudrānvitaṃ śasyate
children.translated_text: in equal parts, powdered and placed in an iron vessel, mixed with honey, is recommended
for itching, <s>arman</s> (pterygium), eye disease, blood-related disorders, <s>rāji</s>, <s>timira</s> (dimness), and as an application for <s>pilla</s> (membrane growth). // Yś_53 //
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), cream of curd (<s>dadhi</s>), <s>kapha</s>, bark (<s>tvak</s>), <s>sevya</s> (vetiver), <s>gorocanā</s> (ox-bile),
<s>māṃsī</s> (spikenard), sandalwood (<s>candana</s>), conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), <s>patra</s> (bay leaf), chalk (<s>girimṛt</s>), <s>tālī</s>, and <s>puṣpāñjana</s> (flower collyrium) —

children.text: sarvair eva samāṃśam añjanam idaṃ śastaṃ sadā cakṣuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: all in equal parts — this collyrium (<s>añjana</s>) is always recommended for the eyes,
removing itching, discharge, impurities, tears, bleeding, pain, <s>pilla</s> (membrane growth), <s>arman</s> (pterygium), and <s>śukra</s> (corneal opacity). // Yś_54 //
A decoction of <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus), <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum), <s>indradāru</s> (Cedrus deodara), <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (Picrorhiza),

children.text: gomūtrasiddho madhunā ca yuktaḥ peyo galavyādhiṣu sarvajeṣu // Yś_55 //
children.translated_text: prepared with cow's urine and combined with honey, should be drunk for all types of throat diseases. // Yś_55 //

children.text: yavāgrajaṃ tejavatīṃ sapāṭhāṃ rasāñjanaṃ dāruniśāṃ sakṛṣṇām /
children.translated_text: <s>Yavāgraja</s> (barley sprouts), <s>tejavatī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), <s>rasāñjana</s> (Berberis extract), <s>dāruniśā</s> (tree turmeric), with black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>) —

children.text: kṣaudreṇa kuryād guṭikāṃ mukhena tāṃ dhārayet sarvagalāmayeṣu // Yś_56 //
children.translated_text: one should make a pill with honey and hold it in the mouth for all throat diseases. // Yś_56 //
A decoction of <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora), fresh <s>sumanā</s> (jasmine) shoots, <s>drākṣā</s> (grapes), <s>yavāsa</s>, and <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits),

children.text: kṣaudreṇa yuktaḥ kavalagraho 'yaṃ mukhasya pākaṃ śamayaty udīrṇam // Yś_57 //
children.translated_text: combined with honey as a mouth gargle (<s>kavalagraha</s>) — this alleviates severe inflammatory conditions (<s>pāka</s>) of the mouth. // Yś_57 //

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ dārvī lodhram abdaṃ samaṅgā pāṭhā tiktā tejanī pītikā ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos), <s>abda</s> (mustard), <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), <s>tiktā</s> (bitter herbs), <s>tejanī</s>, and <s>pītikā</s> —

children.text: cūrṇaṃ śastaṃ gharṣaṇaṃ tad dvijānāṃ raktasrāvaṃ hanti kaṇḍūrujaṃ ca // Yś_58 //
children.translated_text: this powder is recommended as a tooth-rubbing preparation; it destroys bleeding, itching, and pain of the teeth. // Yś_58 //
With <s>sauvīra</s> (vinegar), the juices of fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>) and citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>) flesh, <s>guggulu</s> (resin), and rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>),

children.text: paktvā tu tailaṃ kaṭukaṃ niṣiñcet tat karṇayoḥ karṇarujopaśāntyai // Yś_59 //
children.translated_text: having cooked an oil that is pungent, one should pour it into the ears for the alleviation of ear pain. // Yś_59 //
With <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda), neem (<s>nimba</s>), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>parpaṭa</s>, <s>phala</s> (fruit), <s>śrīcavya</s>, <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), and water,
bitter herbs (<s>tikta</s>), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), <s>durālabhā</s>, the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), <s>trāyantī</s>, and sandalwood (<s>candana</s>) —
ghee prepared with these is useful in disorders above the clavicle, diseases of the nose, eye pain, and similar conditions,
as well as in skin diseases, fever, abscess, wound pain, and corneal opacity (<s>śukra</s>). // Yś_60 //
<s>Dārvī</s> (Berberis), <s>parpaṭa</s>, neem (<s>nimba</s>), <s>vatsaka</s> (Holarrhena), black pepper (<s>kaṇā</s>), <s>duḥsparśa</s>, licorice (<s>yaṣṭī</s>), and <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda),
<s>trāyantī</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>kaṭukā</s> (Picrorhiza), <s>bhūnimba</s> (Andrographis), and <s>raktāmbudā</s> —

children.text: eṣāṃ kalkakaṣāyasādhitam idaṃ sarpiḥ praśastaṃ dṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: ghee prepared with the paste and decoction of these is recommended for the eyes,
in diseases arising from <s>pitta</s> (bile) and blood, in corneal opacity (<s>śukra</s>), dimness of vision (<s>timira</s>), and in disorders above [the clavicle]. // Yś_61 //

children.text: śuklairaṇḍān mūlam athogrā śatapuṣpā puṣpodbhūtaṃ yac ca bṛhatyās tagaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The root of white castor (<s>śukla-eraṇḍa</s>), the fierce <s>śatapuṣpā</s> (dill), the flower of <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), and <s>tagara</s> (valerian) —

children.text: tailaṃ siddhaṃ taiḥ sapayaskais timiraghnaṃ nasyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vyādhiṣu cordhveṣv apareṣu // Yś_62 //
children.translated_text: oil prepared with these together with milk destroys dimness of vision (<s>timira</s>); it is the best nasal medication (<s>nasya</s>) for diseases above [the clavicle] and for other conditions. // Yś_62 //
In a decoction of <s>muṣkaka</s> ash, one should cast conch shell burnt in the flame of fire;

children.text: tat tenaiva punar jalena vipacet kṣāraṃ sa taile vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: then one should cook that very water again to obtain an alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>) — this is the procedure [to prepare] the oil;

children.text: yuñjyāt tad vraṇaduṣṭiṣu vraṇarujāsv arśassu nāḍīṣu ca
children.translated_text: one should apply it in wound infections, wound pain, hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>), fistulae (<s>nāḍī</s>),

children.text: tvagdoṣeṣu bhagaṃdareṣu vividhe kaṇṭhāmaye ca sthire // Yś_63 //
children.translated_text: skin diseases, fistula-in-ano (<s>bhagaṃdara</s>), and in various chronic throat diseases. // Yś_63 //

With turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), licorice (<s>yaṣṭīmadhu</s>), <s>padmaka</s> (Prunus), blue lotus (<s>utpala</s>), <s>priyaṅgu</s> (Callicarpa), <s>kāsāvara</s>, <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos), and sandalwood (<s>candana</s>),

children.text: vipācya tailaṃ payasā prayojayet kṣateṣu saṃropaṇadāhanāśanam // Yś_64 //
children.translated_text: having cooked an oil with milk, one should apply it to wounds — it promotes healing and destroys burning sensation. // Yś_64 //

With equal parts of jasmine (<s>jātī</s>), neem (<s>nimba</s>), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd) leaf, <s>kaṭukā</s> (Picrorhiza), <s>dārvī</s> (Berberis), turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), <s>sārivā</s> (Hemidesmus),
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), <s>abhaya</s> (Terminalia chebula), beeswax (<s>siktham</s>), copper sulfate (<s>tuttha</s>), licorice (<s>madhuka</s>), and <s>naktāhva</s> (night-jasmine) seeds —

children.text: sarpiḥ siddham anena sūkṣmavadanā marmāśritāḥ srāvino
children.translated_text: ghee prepared with these — by this [application], wounds that have fine openings, are located at vital points (<s>marma</s>), are discharging,

children.text: gambhīrāḥ sarujā vraṇāḥ sagatikāḥ śudhyanti rohanti ca // Yś_65 //
children.translated_text: deep, painful, and with sinuses — are purified and heal. // Yś_65 //

children.text: śirīṣapuṣpaṃ svarasena bhāvitaṃ sahasrakṛtvo maricaṃ sitāhvayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śirīṣa</s> (Albizzia) flower macerated in its own juice a thousand times, and white pepper (<s>sitāhvaya</s>) —

children.text: prayojayed añjanapānanāvanair vimohitānām api sarpadaṃśinām // Yś_66 //
children.translated_text: should be employed as collyrium, drink, and nasal medication for those bitten by serpents, even when stupefied. // Yś_66 //

children.text: mayūrapittena tu taṇḍulīyakaṃ kākāṇḍayuktaṃ prapibed analpam /
children.translated_text: <s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus) mixed with peacock bile and <s>kākāṇḍa</s> (Abrus seeds) should be drunk in generous quantity;

children.text: viṣāṇi saṃstāvarajaṅgamāni sopadravāṇy apy acireṇa hanti // Yś_67 //
children.translated_text: it destroys poisons — both vegetable (<s>sthāvara</s>) and animal (<s>jaṅgama</s>) — along with their complications, quickly. // Yś_67 //

children.text: tailaṃ tilānāṃ palalaṃ guḍaṃ ca kṣīraṃ tathārkaṃ samam eva pītam /
children.translated_text: Sesame oil (<s>taila</s>), sesame cake (<s>palala</s>), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), milk, and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) in equal parts, drunk together —

children.text: ālarkam ugraṃ viṣam āśu hanti sadyodbhavaṃ vāyur ivābhravṛndam // Yś_68 //
children.translated_text: swiftly destroys the fierce poison of a rabid [dog] (<s>ālarka</s>), just as wind [disperses] a mass of clouds. // Yś_68 //
Soot from a house (<s>āgāradhūma</s>), combined with buffalo bile (<s>mahiṣākṣa</s>), <s>vājigandhā</s> (Ashwagandha), ghee, and <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus),

children.text: gomūtrapiṣṭo hy agado nihanti viṣāṇi saṃsthāvarajaṅgamāni // Yś_69 //
children.translated_text: ground with cow's urine — this antidote (<s>agada</s>) destroys poisons, both vegetable (<s>sthāvara</s>) and animal (<s>jaṅgama</s>). // Yś_69 //
<s>Māṃsī</s> (spikenard), <s>sevyā</s> (vetiver), <s>alaka</s>, <s>untī</s>, aquatic stone (<s>jalajaladaśilā</s>), <s>rocanā</s> (ox-bile), lotus filaments (<s>padmakeśī</s>),
<s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>caṇḍā</s>, turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>), <s>gada</s>, white indigo (<s>sitapalitā</s>), <s>asṛglatā</s> (Laccifer), <s>padmaka</s> (Prunus), and <s>ailā</s> (cardamom) —
in equal parts, with one-eighth <s>gaurā</s> and four parts <s>ibhakusuma</s> — these collyrium sticks suitable for all purposes,
called '<s>Candrodaya</s>' (Moonrise), as antidotes destroy sorcery (<s>kṛtyā</s>), ill-fortune (<s>alakṣmī</s>), evil spirits (<s>piśāca</s>), fever, and poison. // Yś_70 //
White mustard (<s>siddhārtha</s>), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>śirīṣa</s> (Albizzia), <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora),
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), the two turmeric varieties (<s>rajanīdvaya</s>), the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), and <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) —
this antidote (<s>agada</s>), ground with goat's urine, is recommended for the removal of all seizures (<s>graha</s>),
destroying sorcery (<s>kṛtyā</s>), madness (<s>unmāda</s>), evil spirits (<s>piśāca</s>), and demons (<s>rākṣasa</s>), when employed through drinking and other methods. // Yś_71 //
With cotton-plant bones (<s>karpāsāsthi</s>), peacock feathers (<s>mayūrapatra</s>), <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), <s>nirmālya</s> (discarded offering flowers), <s>piṇḍītaka</s>,
bark (<s>tvak</s>), bamboo (<s>vaṃśī</s>), <s>vṛṣadaṃśa</s>, dung (<s>viṭ</s>), chaff (<s>tuṣa</s>), <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), hair (<s>keśa</s>), and snake slough (<s>ahinirmocaka</s>),
<s>gośṛṅgī</s>, human tooth (<s>dvipadanta</s>), <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), and black pepper (<s>marica</s>) — all in equal parts, a fumigation (<s>dhūpa</s>) is prepared;
it is declared to destroy <s>Skanda</s>-seizure, madness (<s>unmāda</s>), evil spirits (<s>piśāca</s>), demons (<s>rākṣasa</s>), spirit possession (<s>surāveśa</s>), and fever. // Yś_72 //

With the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), cardamom (<s>dala</s>), saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), <s>granthika</s>, alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>), <s>siṃhī</s>, turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (Saussurea), white mustard (<s>siddhārtha</s>), water, and <s>śakrāhvaya</s>,

white garlic (<s>sitalaśuna</s>), fruit, <s>trikoṣīra</s>, <s>tiktā</s> (bitter herbs), <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), copper sulfate (<s>tuttha</s>), licorice (<s>yaṣṭī</s>), <s>balā</s> (Sida), red realgar (<s>lohitākhyāśilā</s>), and <s>padmaka</s> (Prunus),
curd (<s>dadhi</s>), valerian (<s>tagara</s>), <s>madhūkasāra</s>, <s>priyāhvā</s>, <s>viṣākhyā</s>, <s>viṣā</s>, <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s>, with <s>cavya</s> and <s>amara</s>, made into a paste —

children.text: ghṛtam anavam aśeṣamūtrāmbusiddhaṃ smṛtaṃ bhūtarāvaṃ tu pānena tat syād grahaghnaṃ param // Yś_73 //
children.translated_text: fresh ghee prepared with all types of urine and water is known as '<s>Bhūtarāva</s>' (Terror of Demons); taken by drinking, it is the supreme destroyer of spirit-seizures (<s>graha</s>). // Yś_73 //
<s>gadaśuka</s>, <s>tarupuṣpabīja</s>, water, licorice (<s>yaṣṭī</s>), <s>adrikarṇī</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>bilva</s> (Aegle) —
in equal parts, made into a paste, prepared with the urine group — this ghee,

children.text: vidhivinihitam āśu sarvaiḥ kramair yojitaṃ hanti sarvagrahonmādakuṣṭhajvarāṃs tan mahābhūtarāvaṃ smṛtam // Yś_74 //
children.translated_text: properly administered and applied by all methods swiftly, destroys all seizures (<s>graha</s>), madness (<s>unmāda</s>), skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), and fever — it is known as '<s>Mahābhūtarāva</s>' (Great Terror of Demons). // Yś_74 //

body.translated_text:
<s>Nata</s>, <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), white mustard (<s>siddhārtha</s>), <s>siṃhī</s>, turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), the pair (<s>yug</s>), <s>latārohiṇī</s>,
<s>phalakhadira</s> (Acacia), the three pungents (<s>kaṭutrikā</s>), <s>kāṇḍa</s>, <s>dāru</s> (Cedrus), <s>krimighna</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, <s>amara</s>, <s>aṅkollaka</s>, <s>kośātakī</s> (Luffa), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), neem (<s>nimba</s>), water, and <s>indrāhvaya</s> —

children.text: dārvī haridrā kuṭajasya bījaṃ siṃhī ca yaṣṭīmadhukaṃ ca tulyam /
children.translated_text: <s>Dārvī</s> (Berberis), turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>), the seed of <s>kuṭaja</s> (Holarrhena), <s>siṃhī</s>, and licorice (<s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s>) in equal parts —

children.text: kvāthaḥ śiśoḥ stanyakṛte ca doṣe sarvātisāreṣu ca sarvajeṣu // Yś_75 //
children.translated_text: this decoction is for disorders caused by the breast-milk of an infant and for all types of diarrhea (<s>atisāra</s>) of every origin. // Yś_75 //

children.text: bilvaṃ ca puṣpāṇi ca dhātakīnāṃ jalaṃ salodhraṃ gajapippalī ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Bilva</s> (Aegle), flowers of <s>dhātakī</s> (Woodfordia), water with <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos), and <s>gajapippalī</s> (large long pepper) —

children.text: kvāthāvalehau madhunā vimiśrau bāleṣu yojyāv atisāriteṣu // Yś_76 //
children.translated_text: the decoction and electuary mixed with honey should be used for children suffering from diarrhea. // Yś_76 //

children.text: śṛṅgīṃ sakṛṣṇātiviṣāṃ vicūrṇya lehaṃ vidadhyān madhunā śiśūnām /
children.translated_text: Having powdered <s>śṛṅgī</s> (Pistacia), black pepper (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), and <s>ativiṣā</s> (Aconitum), one should prepare an electuary (<s>leha</s>) with honey for infants —

children.text: kāsajvaracchardibhir arditānāṃ samākṣikāṃ cātiviṣām athaikām // Yś_77 //
children.translated_text: for those afflicted by cough, fever, and vomiting, one should administer <s>ativiṣā</s> combined with honey.
A bronze vessel of <s>dhātrī</s> (amla) powder, mixed with its own juice, equal portions of honey and ghee,
combined with eight <s>prasṛtis</s> of <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper), iron powder, and sugar, placed in a heap of ashes—

children.text: varṣānte tat samaśnan bhavati vipalito rūpavarṇaprabhāvī
children.translated_text: one who eats this at the end of the rains becomes grey-haired [yet restored to] beauty, complexion, and vigor,
free from disease, endowed with intelligence, wisdom, memory, eloquence, strength, firmness, and vitality.
The three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>) combined with <s>yaṣṭī</s> (licorice), <s>tugā</s>, rock salt, and <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper),

children.text: āyuḥpradā vṛṣyatamātimedhyā bhavej jarāvyādhivināśanī ca // Yś_79 //
children.translated_text: along with sugar, become life-giving, supremely aphrodisiac, highly intellect-promoting, and destructive of old age and disease.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ śvadaṃṣṭrāmalakāmṛtānāṃ lihet sasarpir madhunā ca yuktam /
children.translated_text: One should lick the powder of <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (gokṣura), <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>guḍūcī</s>, mixed with ghee and honey;

children.text: vṛṣyaḥ sthiraḥ śāntavikāraduḥkhaḥ samāśataṃ jīvati kṛṣṇakeśaḥ // Yś_80 //
children.translated_text: one becomes virile, firm, with ailments and suffering pacified, lives a hundred years with black hair.

children.text: nimbasya tailaṃ prakṛtistham evaṃ nasyāṃ niṣiktaṃ vidhinā yathāvat /
children.translated_text: The oil of <s>nimba</s> (neem), in its natural state, administered as nasal drops according to the proper method—

children.text: māsena tat kṣīraghṛtopayojyaṃ jarāprabhūtaṃ palitaṃ nihanti // Yś_81 //
children.translated_text: used with milk and ghee for a month, it destroys grey hair caused by old age.

children.text: gokṣurakaḥ kṣurakaḥ śatamūlī vānari nāgabalātibalā ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Gokṣuraka</s>, <s>kṣuraka</s>, <s>śatamūlī</s> (asparagus), <s>vānarī</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>—

children.text: cūrṇam idaṃ payasā niśi peyaṃ yasya gṛhe pramadāśatam asti // Yś_82 //
children.translated_text: this powder should be drunk with milk at night by one who has a hundred women in his house.

children.text: madhukāṃ madhunā ghṛtena ca pralihan kṣīram anuprayojayet /
children.translated_text: By licking <s>madhuka</s> (licorice) with honey and ghee, and following it with milk,

children.text: labhate ca na dhātusaṃkṣayaṃ pramadānāṃ ca śataṃ ca gacchati // Yś_83 //
children.translated_text: one does not suffer depletion of bodily tissues, and one can visit a hundred women.
A decoction of <s>yaṣṭī</s> (licorice) mixed with the best salt and a paste of <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (pepper), and fruit,

children.text: sakṣaudram etad vamanaṃ prayojyaṃ ghrāṇāsyakaṇṭhaśravaṇāmayeṣu // Yś_84 //
children.translated_text: combined with honey—this emetic should be employed in diseases of the nose, mouth, throat, and ears.
<s>Harītakī</s> decocted in <s>suvīra</s> (vinegar), mixed with powders of <s>dantī</s>, <s>aṅghri</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, and emblic myrobalan,

children.text: virecanaṃ sorubutailam etan niratyayaṃ yojyam athāmayaghnam // Yś_85 //
children.translated_text: combined with castor oil—this purgative is safe and disease-destroying, to be administered.
<s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>rāṭha</s> (castor), the three fruits, <s>guḍūcī</s>, the five roots, <s>balā</s>—
combined with a meat broth, with portions of oil, salt, honey, ghee, and <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery),
mixed with pastes of <s>puṣpāhva</s>, <s>ghana</s> (musta), <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>vacā</s>—
this enema, combined with sour gruel, milk, and urine, is beneficial for <s>vāta</s> diseases.
Oil cooked with a decoction and paste of <s>balā</s> and <s>sugandhī</s>, prepared with milk, curds, husk-water, rice-wash, and vinegar,
likewise with <s>sahacara</s>, <s>saraṇya</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>avārī</s>—each separately cooked—destroys wind in retention enemas.

children.text: nasyaṃ vidadhyād guḍanāgaraṃ vā sasaindhavāṃ māgadhikām athovā /
children.translated_text: One should administer as nasal drops either <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) with <s>nāgara</s> (ginger), or <s>māgadhikā</s> (long pepper) with rock salt—
in diseases of the nose, mouth, jaw, face, arms, back, head, eyes, throat, and ears.

children.text: śreṣṭhaḥ parpaṭako jvareṣu vihitas tṛṣṇāsu pañcāmliko
children.translated_text: The best in fevers is <s>parpaṭaka</s>; in thirst, the five-sour formula;

children.text: lājā cchardiṣu vastijeṣu girijo meheṣu dhātrīrasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>lājā</s> (parched rice) in vomiting; <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) in urinary diseases; <s>dhātrī</s> (amla) juice in <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders);

children.text: rāsnā vātagadeṣu mūtram udare plīhāmaye pippalī
children.translated_text: <s>rāsnā</s> in <s>vāta</s> diseases; urine in abdominal disorders; <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) in splenic disease;

children.text: saṃdhāne kṛmihā viṣe śukataruḥ śophe tathā gugguluḥ // Yś_89 //
children.translated_text: worm-killers in wound-healing; <s>śukrataru</s> in poisoning; and <s>guggulu</s> in swelling.

children.text: vṛṣo 'śrapitte kuṭajo 'tisāre bhallātam arśassu gareṣu hema /
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣa</s> (vasaka) in blood-bile disorders; <s>kuṭaja</s> in diarrhea; <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut) in hemorrhoids; gold in toxic conditions;

children.text: sthūleṣu dāruḥ kṛmiṣu krimighnaṃ harītakī pāṇḍugadeṣu śasyate // Yś_90 //
children.translated_text: <s>dāru</s> (cedar) in obesity; <s>krimighna</s> (worm-killer) in parasites; <s>harītakī</s> is praised in jaundice.

children.text: akṣyāmayeṣu triphalā vadanti śūleṣu sarveṣu tathā rasonam /
children.translated_text: <s>Triphalā</s> is proclaimed for eye diseases; garlic for all colicky pains;

children.text: kuṣṭheṣu nityaṃ khadirasya sāraṃ sarveṣu kāseṣu nidigdhikāṃ ca // Yś_91 //
children.translated_text: the heartwood of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) always for skin diseases; and <s>nidigdhikā</s> (kaṇṭakārī) for all types of cough.

children.text: śaṃsanti vājīkaraṇe śvadaṃṣṭrām uraḥkṣate nāgabalā balāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: They recommend <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> (gokṣura) for aphrodisiacs; <s>nāgabalā</s> and <s>balā</s> for chest wounds;

children.text: rasāyaneṣv āmalakaṃ sadevagraheṣu rogeṣu śilāhvayaṃ ca // Yś_92 //
children.translated_text: <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) for rejuvenation; and <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) for diseases caused by gods and planetary afflictions.

children.text: ity ete vidhivihitāḥ prasiddhayogāḥ siddhyarthaṃ vinigaditā bhiṣagvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: These well-established formulations have been prescribed methodically, expounded for the success of the best physicians;

children.text: dṛṣṭvaitān katham acikitsako 'pi yuñjyād ity arthaṃ punar api vakṣyate 'tra kiṃcit // Yś_93 //
children.translated_text: having seen these, how even a non-physician might apply them—for this purpose, something more will now be stated here.
Through retention [of natural urges], fasting, wakefulness, loud speaking, exertion, travel, pungent, bitter, astringent, and dry foods,

children.text: cintāvyavāyabhayalaṅghanaśokaśītair vāyuḥ prakopam upayāti ghanāgame ca // Yś_94 //
children.translated_text: anxiety, sexual intercourse, fear, hunger-fasting, grief, cold, and also during the onset of rains—<s>vāta</s> becomes aggravated.
Through pungent, sour, alcoholic, salty, hot, burning, sharp foods, anger, fire, sun exposure, exhaustion, dried vegetables,

children.text: kṣārādyajīrṇaviṣamāśanabhojanaś ca pittaṃ prakopam upayāti ghanātyaye ca // Yś_95 //
children.translated_text: alkaline substances, indigestion, irregular eating, and food [of such nature]—<s>pitta</s> becomes aggravated, and also at the end of the rains.
Through daytime sleep, sweet, cool, fat, meat, heavy, sour, slimy, sesame, sugarcane, and milk products,

children.text: snigdhātitṛptilavaṇodakapānabhakṣaiḥ śleṣmā prakopam upayāti tathā vasante // Yś_96 //
children.translated_text: unctuous, over-satiation, salty, excessive water-drinking, and [such] foods—<s>kapha</s> becomes aggravated, and also in spring.

children.text: ity evam ete kramaśo dviśo vā doṣāḥ pravṛddhā yugapat trayo vā /
children.translated_text: Thus these <s>doṣas</s> (humors), aggravated sequentially, in pairs,

children.text: kurvanti rogān vividhān śarīre saṃkhyātu saṃjnāvigatān anekān // Yś_97 //
children.translated_text: or simultaneously all three, produce various diseases in the body—innumerable, with names beyond counting.
Roughness, contraction, pricking pain, colic, dark discoloration, body aches, fracture-like movements,

children.text: suptatvaśītatvakharatvaśoṣān karmāṇi vāyoḥ pravadanti tajjñāḥ // Yś_98 //
children.translated_text: numbness, coldness, hardness, and desiccation—these the experts declare to be the actions of <s>vāta</s>.
Discharge, sweating, burning, redness, foul smell, moistness, digestion, and irritation,

children.text: pralāpamūrchabhramapītabhāvān pittasya karmāṇi vadanti tajjñāḥ // Yś_99 //
children.translated_text: delirium, fainting, dizziness, and yellowish discoloration—these the experts declare to be the actions of <s>pitta</s>.
Whiteness, coldness, heaviness, itching, unctuousness, coating, rigidity, adhesion,

children.text: utsekasaṃghātacirakriyāś ca kaphasya karmāṇi vadanti tajjnāḥ // Yś_100 //
children.translated_text: nausea, congestion, and slowness of action—these the experts declare to be the actions of <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: etāni liṅgāni ca tatkṛtānāṃ sarvāmayānām api naikanāmnām /
children.translated_text: These are the signs of all diseases caused by those [<s>doṣas</s>], bearing many names;

children.text: kaścid bhavet prāptiviśeṣa eṣāṃ saṃjñāntaraṃ yena tu saṃprayānti // Yś_101 //
children.translated_text: some special combination of these may occur, whereby they come to bear different names.
Through lethargy, drowsiness, impurity of the heart, non-movement of <s>doṣas</s>, absence of hunger, urine [abnormality],
heaviness of the abdomen, loss of appetite, and numbness—they describe a disease accompanied by <s>āma</s> (undigested matter).
Through unctuous, hot, firm, aphrodisiac, strengthening, mildly salty, sweet, sour, oily, sun-exposure,
bathing, anointing, enemas, meat, wine, massage, and rubbing,
oleation, sudation, decoction enema, nasal drops, pacifying treatments, oil poultices, and the like—
this regimen of drink, food, activities, and medicine leads <s>vāta</s> to pacification.
Bitter, sweet, astringent, cooling, wind, shade, night, fanning,
moonlight, earth, house, water-spray, rain, cloud, contact with a woman's body,
ghee, milk, purgation, affusion, bloodletting, application of pastes, and the like—

children.text: pānāhāravihārabheṣajam idaṃ pittaṃ praśāntiṃ nayet // Yś_104 //
children.translated_text: this regimen of drink, food, activities, and medicine leads <s>pitta</s> to pacification.
Dry, alkaline, astringent, bitter, pungent, exercise, expectorating,
sexual intercourse, walking, fighting, staying awake, water-play, foot-stamping,
smoke inhalation, very hot [substances], head-purgation, emesis, sudation, fasting, and the like—

children.text: pānāhāravihārabhaiṣajam idaṃ śleṣmānam ugraṃ jayet // Yś_105 //
children.translated_text: this regimen of drink, food, activities, and medicine conquers severe <s>kapha</s>.
One should conquer <s>āma</s> through fasting, <s>kola</s> (jujube) gruel, light food, thin soup, water, and bitter broths,

children.text: virūkṣaṇasvedanapācanaiś ca saṃśodhanair ūrdhvam adhas tathā ca // Yś_106 //
children.translated_text: through drying, sudation, digestive treatments, and purification both upward and downward.
In winter, the rains, and the cool season, <s>vāta</s> [is aggravated]; <s>pitta</s> in autumn and the hot season;

children.text: kaphasya kopaḥ kusumāgame ca kurvanti tad vai vihitaṃ yathaiṣām // Yś_107 //
children.translated_text: <s>kapha</s> becomes aggravated at the onset of spring; one should treat them accordingly as prescribed.

children.text: kaphasya kope vamanaṃ sanasyaṃ virecanaṃ pittabhave vikāre /
children.translated_text: When <s>kapha</s> is aggravated, emesis with nasal drops [is indicated]; purgation in disorders arising from <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: vātātmake vastim udāharanti saṃsargaje 'pi vyatimiśram etat // Yś_108 //
children.translated_text: in conditions of <s>vāta</s> nature, they prescribe enema; in combined conditions, mixed treatment is appropriate.
<s>Vāta</s> is pacified by sour, oily, salty, and sweet food and drink; <s>pitta</s> by sweet, bitter, astringent, and cooling;

children.text: śleṣmāpi tiktakaṭurūkṣakaṣāyatīkṣṇair āmaṃ praśāntim upayānty apatarpaṇena // Yś_109 //
children.translated_text: <s>kapha</s> by bitter, pungent, dry, astringent, and sharp; and <s>āma</s> subsides through depletive therapy.

children.text: buddhvaitad anyad api yat tad anuktam atra yuktyā svayaṃ samadhigamya yathānurūpam /
children.translated_text: Having understood this, whatever else is left unsaid here,

children.text: rogeṣu bheṣajam analpamatir vidadhyāc chāstraṃ hi kiṃcid upadeśalavaṃ karoti // Yś_110 //
children.translated_text: having ascertained it oneself through reasoning and as is appropriate, a physician of no small intellect should administer medicine for diseases; for a treatise provides only a hint of instruction.

children.text: guṇādhikaṃ yogaśataṃ nibadhya prāptaṃ mayā puṇyam anuttaraṃ yat /
children.translated_text: Having composed the <s>Yogaśataka</s> (Hundred Formulations) rich in virtues, whatever unsurpassed merit I have obtained—

children.text: nānāprakārāmayanīḍabhūtaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat tena bhavatv arogam // Yś_111 //
children.translated_text: may the entire world, which is a nest of manifold diseases, become free from illness through that merit.
